blurb: A retail set. The court must decide which item gives it its essential character.
reference_excerpt: The classification of the gift set must be broken down into its individual components as per the ruling. The gift set includes a working watch, which is classified under HTS code 9102.11.10 due to its quartz analog movement and gold-plated case and strap. The tweezers are classified under HTS code 8203.20.2000 as they fall under the category of pliers and similar tools. The nail file and nail clipper are classified under HTS code 8214.20.3000, which pertains to manicure or pedicure sets and instruments. Lastly, the cuticle scissors are classified under HTS code 8213.00.9000, which covers scissors and similar shears valued over a certain threshold.

gri_path: GRI 1: the watch falls in heading 9102. The manicure tools fall in 8214, or 8203 for the tweezers and 8213 for the scissors. No single heading covers the whole set.
GRI 3(a): each heading names only part of the set, so they are equally specific.
GRI 3(b): a retail set of unrelated items is classified by the component that gives essential character. I assumed this is the watch, based on its likely higher value and function.
GRI 6: I took 9102.11.25 as a placeholder subheading. Display type, movement, case plating and jewel count are unknown.
